page: Amazon Web Services r3.2xlarge is a previous-generation, memory-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical execution cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 61.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.62 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware resources include a bundled 160 GB local SSD for high-speed scratch space, a 1 Gbps baseline network interface, and no hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the older architectural profile of the Ivy Bridge platform. Single-core performance is limited, with Geekbench single-core scoring 726.0 and stress-ng single-core recording 1285.69, placing it in the bottom tiers of modern virtual compute. Multi-core performance scales to average levels, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 7427.64 and multi-threaded decompression at 27.09 GB/sec. Uncached memory throughput sustains 52.14 GB/sec for sequential reads and 40.68 GB/sec for writes. The absence of contemporary instruction sets such as AVX-512, BMI2, and FMA restricts compute and vector processing potential.

The r3.2xlarge offers functional resource density for workloads demanding high memory capacity and local high-speed disk caching without needing state-of-the-art CPU throughput. It is technically suitable for in-memory databases, Redis caches, batch ETL operations, and mid-tier relational database management systems. Modern compute-bound tasks, heavy compilation, and large language model inference will experience architectural bottlenecks due to the legacy CPU generation.
